checks: Translate the (d−1)-dimensional F to height zero. Its positive section measure f and the full-dimensional D meet the accepted section lemma. The root h=|D_t|^(1/(d−1)) is positive and concave at interior heights, and its (d−1)st integral is U.

For binomial degree p, multiplying the moment bound by f^((d−1−p)/(d−1)) yields P r^p/(p+1), before its binomial coefficient. The degrees zero and d−1 give P and U exactly. Expansions give the stated square-root coefficient in d=3 and both mixed terms in d=4.

The height-t cone has sections trF in fractional height t, so section roots are affine and F+(tr)F=(1+tr)F. Its volume is Pr^(d−1)/d, giving equality. For d=2 addition of intervals makes the reserve exact for arbitrary pairs.

Balanced simplex normals make (1−v_i·x)/(d+1) the barycentric coordinates. The facet pyramid from 0 has volume b/(d+1) and height 1/||v_i||. The proper A cut supplies width H_i/||v_i||. Its sum with the actual B facet lies in 2K∩{v_i·x≥0}; the factor is 2^d and the endpoint B trace is d-volume null.

When the stated three bases carry all positive mass, Q=U_i+q_i. In d=3 substitution adds 8U_i to U_i+P_i+sqrt(3U_iP_i), giving the exact coefficient 9. Source b69ebda3a2e6d72a §§3–4 (2)–(6) matches these scopes and constants.

dependencies.hypotheses: D is full dimensional and F has positive (d−1)-measure in its fixed height plane. The exact sections of their sum and the sectional Brunn–Minkowski lower integral apply in every stated dimension.
